access.edition_or_version: The Devotional Poems of Mirabai, trans. A. J. Alston (Motilal Banarsidass, 1980)

mechanics.tone_relevance: Non-Anglophone anchor for intimate address: the devotional first person addresses Krishna with the intimacy of a lover or companion.
mechanics.point_of_view: First person, addressed to a named beloved deity (Giridhar / the Mountain-lifter); refrain repeats the invocation.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Longing, jealousy, anger at absence, and ecstatic union succeed one another across the songs.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Everyday domestic imagery; sung refrain; internal signature naming the devotee; direct appeal and complaint.
mechanics.intimacy_technique: Intimacy is carried by address and by plain, concrete images of love rather than by literal autobiography.
mechanics.boundary_caveat: The intimate voice is often voiced through a devotional persona (gopi/Radha); this demonstrates addressed interiority and register, not literal self-disclosure.
mechanics.translation_note: Braj Bhasa verse loses musical refrain and idiomatic texture in English; attribution is uncertain because the songs survive orally.
mechanics.copyright_note: Translation copyrighted; poem texts are traditional. Techniques described, no text reproduced.
